Baseline model: robust (Huber) two-part regression on daily kWh — base load estimated from off-production intervals with a degree-day response; production surplus regressed on per-product unit volumes, degree-days and calendar effects. Fitted on the baseline quarter only (no leakage).
Counterfactuals are level translations on the current period's calendar: volume scaled by the total-units ratio, quarterly mix shares, and current weather shifted to the other quarter's mean.
Daily modelled energy is allocated to tariff buckets with the baseline quarter's observed intraday shares (profile-shape stability assumption).
Attribution: Shapley (order-independent, exact); tariff prices looked up per 15-minute interval, so the mid-period tariff change is handled exactly.
limitations: Baseline fit: train R2 1.00, holdout MAPE 6.0%; the residual 'waste' term includes baseline model error of about +0.06 pct points and estimation noise.
The waste component is an unexplained residual in currency terms. It does NOT by itself identify a faulty asset — asset-level claims require corroborating meter evidence.

findings.inferred_cause: Night-time and weekend compressor load staying above its early-quarter level - consistent with a compressed-air leak; requires physical inspection.

idle.note: Findings are measured load patterns plus clearly-labelled inferred causes (never confirmed faults). A repair recommendation is only raised when the bill decomposition also leaves a controllable residual to explain.
